The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has said the President Bola Tinubu-led administration is ushering in a new era in Nigeria’s broadcasting industry through the launch of the Digital Switch-Over platform, FreeTV. He said the platform would expand access to digital television, create opportunities for local content producers and strengthen the broadcasting and creative industries. A statement by the minister’s Special Assistant, Rabiu Ibrahim, said Idris made the remarks on Thursday at the 2026 Annual General Meeting of the Independent Broadcasting Association of Nigeria in Abuja. The minister, who was represented by Ibrahim, said the launch of FreeTV on June 17, 2026, marked a significant milestone in the country’s transition from analogue to digital broadcasting. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, the Federal Government has taken an important step towards modernising the broadcasting sector through the launch of Nigeria’s Digital Switch-Over platform,” he said. He urged stakeholders to create an environment that encouraged investment, promoted local content, protected editorial independence and enabled Nigerian broadcasters to compete in the changing global industry. Idris also commended IBAN for providing a platform for independent broadcasters to engage the government and regulators on issues affecting the sector. He urged the association to sustain its engagement with the government and continue promoting professionalism, innovation and responsible broadcasting. According to him, the next phase of the industry’s development should produce a stronger, more competitive and sustainable broadcasting sector.
